#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

So `assert_shard_manifest.py` asserts the union of shards == all test files (minus excludes). `test/site_geo_crawl_test.dart` exists on disk but isn't in the manifest... yet CI passed.       # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core and
      # nightly.yml.
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

Tool error (bash): # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

So `assert_shard_manifest.py` asserts the union of shards == all test files (minus excludes). `test/site_geo_crawl_test.dart` exists on disk but isn't in the manifest... yet CI passed.       - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})

        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

So `assert_shard_manifest.py` asserts the union of shards == all test files (minus excludes). `test/site_geo_crawl_test.dart` exists on disk but isn't in the manifest... yet CI passed. So either the assert runs with excludes covering test/site, or site tests are excluded somewhere. Let me check how ci.yml invokes assert_shard_manifest and what excludes it passes.

Where is the CORE manifest asserted in ci.yml? The core test step runs `targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ...)` at line 498 — shard_files.py bin-packs files not in the manifest at runtime ("a NEW test file added by a PR needs no manifest edit — shard_files.py bin-packs uncovered files into shards at runtime"). So test/site_geo_crawl_test.dart gets bin-packed into a core shard automatically! That means after removing artifacts from the tree, the crawl test WOULD RUN in core shards against an unbuilt tree and FAIL.

So I must handle: test/site tests cannot run in plain core shards without a built site. Options:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

So `assert_shard_manifest.py` asserts the union of shards == all test files (minus excludes). `test/site_geo_crawl_test.dart` exists on disk but isn't in the manifest... yet CI passed. So either the assert runs with excludes covering test/site, or site tests are excluded somewhere. Let me check how ci.yml invokes assert_shard_manifest and what excludes it passes.

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from shard_files import file_has_tag


def full_suite(root: str, exclude: list, tag=None, exclude_tags=None) -> set:
    out = set()
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True):
        norm = path.replace(os.sep, "/")
        if any(x in norm for x in exclude):
            continue
        if tag is not None:
            # Tag-scoped manifest: the suite IS the tagged files (same
            # matcher the runtime selector bin-packs with).
            if not file_has_tag(path, tag):
                continue
        elif "/integration/" in norm:
            continue
        if exclude_tags and any(file_has_tag(path, t) for t in exclude_tags):
            continue  # gh-1199 AC1: the live boundary shrinks the suite
        out.add(norm)

So test/site_geo_crawl_test.dart gets bin-packed into a core shard automatically! That means after removing artifacts from the tree, the crawl test WOULD RUN in core shards against an unbuilt tree and FAIL.

So I must handle: test/site tests cannot run in plain core shards without a built site. Options:

A. Tag test/site tests with a tag (e.g. `site` or reuse `io`?) and exclude from core shards, run them only in the static job with FA_SITE_ROOT. Tag-scoped exclusion requires shard selection --exclude-tag and llm boundary awareness. There's precedent: browser-ext tag.

Make test/site tests self-sufficient: in setUpAll/main, if generated artifacts missing from siteRoot, build them in-tree first (run `dart scripts/build_site.dart`? from within a test — could invoke the builder API directly since tests import the script? test/site doesn't import the builder... it could).       # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \

blocks.text:
One failure: styles.css missing in the out dir. Why? `_copyStaticSite` walk: `src.listSync(recursive: true)` — with recursive listing, does it include the top-level files of `site/` itself? Yes it should. Hmm — wait, `out.path` is `${root.path}-out` — the out dir is a SIBLING of the temp root, but the temp root is under /tmp... no issue there.

Ah — I see it. In the test, `out = Directory('${root.path}-out')`. `_copyStaticSite(root, outDir)` walks `$root/site`. That includes styles.css → copies to `$outDir/styles.css`... wait no: rel = 'styles.css', dest = '$outDir/styles.css'?? No — dest should be `$outDir/site/styles.css`! rel is relative to `src` = `$root/site`, so copying to `$outDir/$rel` loses the `site/` prefix!

Right: outputs are written at `$target/site/...` (paths are site-relative: 'site/blog/...'). But _copyStaticSite writes to `$outDir/$rel` where rel lacks the 'site/' prefix. Inconsistent. The out dir should contain `site/` subdir (as in FA_SITE_ROOT=$d/site). Fix: dest = `$outDir/site/$rel` and dirs `$outDir/site/$rel`.

{"newText":"      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.
      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)
        run: |
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out "$d"
          FA_SITE_ROOT="$d/site" dart test/site/","oldText":"      # gh-1476 AC5: the GEO layer (static blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml,

      # any hand-edit of generated output or stale artifact after a

Why? The prune checks `expectedPaths.any((p) => p.startsWith('$dir/'))` — dir is 'blog/2026-01-02-one', expectedPaths contains 'blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html'. `'blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html'.startsWith('blog/2026-01-02-one/')` → true. So it shouldn't prune... unless expectedPaths entries lack the prefix. Wait, in the --out case strip='site/', rel gives 'blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html' ✓.

Hmm wait — but `_generatedPageDirs(siteDir)` where siteDir='$base/site'... in the out test, base=outDir. But the OUTPUT was written to '$base/${rel(o)}' = out/blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html ✓. siteDir = out/site?? NO — base = outDir = out.path; siteDir = '$base/site' = out/site — but files are at out/blog! _generatedPageDirs scans out/site/blog — which doesn't exist... but the log shows pruning happened of blog/2026-01-02-one — so it scanned out/blog. That means siteDir was out/blog's parent... 

Oh wait — I see: my edit set `final siteDir = '$base/site';` — that's wrong for out mode now! In out mode, files land directly at $base/blog/..., so generated dirs scan should be at $base. And in-tree, at $root/site. So siteDir should be: outDir ?? '$root/site'. That's what I had before the last edit for siteDir, but the WRITE base must be $root (in-tree) vs $outDir (out). Let me re-fix: base=root (in-tree) / outDir (out) for writes; siteDir = outDir ?? '$root/site' for scanning.

2. **in-tree emit**: still failing at 557 (sitemap at ${root.path}/site/sitemap.xml). base=root, rel full path 'site/sitemap.xml' → writes $root/site/sitemap.xml ✓ should exist... but wait, prune may have deleted?? Prune scans siteDir='$base/site' = root/site, dirs found include 'blog/2026-01-02-one' (just written, has index.html ✓) expectedPaths = full 'site/blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html'; check `p.startsWith('$dir/')` → 'site/blog/...'.startsWith('blog/2026.../') → FALSE → prunes the fresh page! And sitemap? sitemap is a file, not pruned. But the failure is at 557 — the sitemap assertion... Expected true actual false. Hmm — sitemap.xml written at '$base/site/sitemap.xml'... 

wait no, in-tree: `File('$base/${rel(o)}')` = root + '/site/sitemap.xml' ✓. Unless... the fixture also has the stale dir prune... Let me think about why sitemap missing. OH — the previous test failure mode: these tests run in RANDOM order with a shared fixture per test (setUp per test, fresh temp root each). Hmm.

Wait, actually let me recheck: in-tree test — `site.emitSite(root: root.path, outputs: outputs)`. base = root.path. rel = 'site/sitemap.xml'. File: root/site/sitemap.xml written ✓. Then prune: siteDir = '$base/site'... in my CURRENT code after last edit: `final siteDir = '$base/site';` — for in-tree that's root/site ✓. dirs found: blog/2024-01-01-old (stale) and blog/2026-01-02-one (fresh). expectedPaths (strip empty) = 'site/blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html'. startsWith('blog/2026-01-02-one/') false → PRUNE fresh page. Test then checks `File('${root.path}/site/blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html').existsSync()` isTrue at line ~559 and sitemap at 557... 557 is sitemap — hmm expected true actual false?? 

Hold on, 557:9 — after format, line numbers shifted. sed showed line 556 = sitemap expect in previous read? Earlier read showed 554-556: expect sitemap at 556, then blog page at 557-560. Failure at 557:9 → the blog page assertion. OK consistent: fresh page pruned due to path mismatch.

And failure 1 (out prune test): siteDir='$base/site' = out/site — doesn't exist → no dirs found... but log showed pruning of blog/2026-01-02-one in the out test?? The log lines "pruned stale page: blog/2024-01-01-old/" and "blog/2026-01-02-one/" appeared right before in-tree test failure — order: the '❌ prunes stale' group printed, then appstore tests, then "pruned stale page: blog/2024-01-01-old/" + "pruned stale page: blog/2026-01-02-one/" — these are from the IN-TREE test run. So out test: no pruning at all (siteDir wrong), staleOut survived → fail. In-tree test: fresh page pruned (prefix mismatch) → fail at 557.

Fix: 
```dart
final siteDir = outDir ?? '$root/site';  // scan target
final base = outDir ?? root;             // write target
```
Writes: in-tree at root/site/... ✓; out at outDir/blog/... ✓. Scan: in-tree at root/site ✓; out at outDir ✓.

expectedPaths in out mode: stripped 'blog/...' matching dirs 'blog/...' ✓. In-tree: full 'site/blog/...' vs dirs 'blog/...' ✗ — mismatch again for in-tree! Because _generatedPageDirs(siteDir) returns dirs relative to siteDir ('blog/x'), while in-tree expectedPaths are root-relative ('site/blog/x/index.html').

Normalize: make expectedPaths siteDir-relative in both modes:
- in-tree: rel(o) minus 'site/' prefix = 'blog/x/index.html'
- out: rel(o) already stripped.

i.e. `final prefix = 'site/'; siteRelative(o) = o.path.substring(prefix.length)` for BOTH modes (all output paths start with 'site/'). Prune compares against dirs relative to siteDir. Clean:

```dart
void emitSite({required String root, String? outDir, required List<OutputFile> outputs}) {
  final siteDir = outDir ?? '$root/site';
  if (outDir != null) _copyStaticSite(root, outDir);
  for (final o in outputs) {
    final targetPath = outDir != null ? '$outDir/${o.path}' : '$root/${o.path}';
    ...write
  }
  final expectedPaths = {for (final o in outputs) o.path.substring('site/'.length)};
  for (final dir in _generatedPageDirs(siteDir)) {
    if (!expectedPaths.any((p) => p.startsWith('$dir/'))) prune('$siteDir/$dir')
  }
```

For out mode write: '$outDir/${o.path}' would give out/site/blog/... — wrong. So write path: out mode strips 'site/': '$outDir/${o.path.substring('site/'.length)}'; in-tree: '$root/${o.path}'.

messages.preview: Path-prefix mismatches between write target and prune scan. Fixing `emitSite` cleanly:

blocks.text:
Two issues:

1. **"prunes stale generated pages already in the out dir"**: `pruned stale page: blog/2024-01-01-old/` ✓ but then ALSO `pruned stale page: blog/2026-01-02-one/` — the freshly written post page got pruned! Why? The prune checks `expectedPaths.any((p) => p.startsWith('$dir/'))` — dir is 'blog/2026-01-02-one', expectedPaths contains 'blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html'. `'blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html'.startsWith('blog/2026-01-02-one/')` → true. So it shouldn't prune... unless expectedPaths entries lack the prefix. Wait, in the --out case strip='site/', rel gives 'blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html' ✓.

Hmm wait — but `_generatedPageDirs(siteDir)` where siteDir='$base/site'... in the out test, base=outDir. But the OUTPUT was written to '$base/${rel(o)}' = out/blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html ✓. siteDir = out/site?? NO — base = outDir = out.path; siteDir = '$base/site' = out/site — but files are at out/blog! _generatedPageDirs scans out/site/blog — which doesn't exist... but the log shows pruning happened of blog/2026-01-02-one — so it scanned out/blog. That means siteDir was out/blog's parent... 

Oh wait — I see: my edit set `final siteDir = '$base/site';` — that's wrong for out mode now! In out mode, files land directly at $base/blog/..., so generated dirs scan should be at $base. And in-tree, at $root/site. So siteDir should be: outDir ?? '$root/site'. That's what I had before the last edit for siteDir, but the WRITE base must be $root (in-tree) vs $outDir (out). Let me re-fix: base=root (in-tree) / outDir (out) for writes; siteDir = outDir ?? '$root/site' for scanning.

2. **in-tree emit**: still failing at 557 (sitemap at ${root.path}/site/sitemap.xml). base=root, rel full path 'site/sitemap.xml' → writes $root/site/sitemap.xml ✓ should exist... but wait, prune may have deleted?? Prune scans siteDir='$base/site' = root/site, dirs found include 'blog/2026-01-02-one' (just written, has index.html ✓) expectedPaths = full 'site/blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html'; check `p.startsWith('$dir/')` → 'site/blog/...'.startsWith('blog/2026.../') → FALSE → prunes the fresh page! And sitemap? sitemap is a file, not pruned. But the failure is at 557 — the sitemap assertion... Expected true actual false. Hmm — sitemap.xml written at '$base/site/sitemap.xml'... 

wait no, in-tree: `File('$base/${rel(o)}')` = root + '/site/sitemap.xml' ✓. Unless... the fixture also has the stale dir prune... Let me think about why sitemap missing. OH — the previous test failure mode: these tests run in RANDOM order with a shared fixture per test (setUp per test, fresh temp root each). Hmm.

Wait, actually let me recheck: in-tree test — `site.emitSite(root: root.path, outputs: outputs)`. base = root.path. rel = 'site/sitemap.xml'. File: root/site/sitemap.xml written ✓. Then prune: siteDir = '$base/site'... in my CURRENT code after last edit: `final siteDir = '$base/site';` — for in-tree that's root/site ✓. dirs found: blog/2024-01-01-old (stale) and blog/2026-01-02-one (fresh). expectedPaths (strip empty) = 'site/blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html'. startsWith('blog/2026-01-02-one/') false → PRUNE fresh page. Test then checks `File('${root.path}/site/blog/2026-01-02-one/index.html').existsSync()` isTrue at line ~559 and sitemap at 557... 557 is sitemap — hmm expected true actual false?? 

Hold on, 557:9 — after format, line numbers shifted. sed showed line 556 = sitemap expect in previous read? Earlier read showed 554-556: expect sitemap at 556, then blog page at 557-560. Failure at 557:9 → the blog page assertion. OK consistent: fresh page pruned due to path mismatch.

And failure 1 (out prune test): siteDir='$base/site' = out/site — doesn't exist → no dirs found... but log showed pruning of blog/2026-01-02-one in the out test?? The log lines "pruned stale page: blog/2024-01-01-old/" and "blog/2026-01-02-one/" appeared right before in-tree test failure — order: the '❌ prunes stale' group printed, then appstore tests, then "pruned stale page: blog/2024-01-01-old/" + "pruned stale page: blog/2026-01-02-one/" — these are from the IN-TREE test run. So out test: no pruning at all (siteDir wrong), staleOut survived → fail. In-tree test: fresh page pruned (prefix mismatch) → fail at 557.

Fix: 
```dart
final siteDir = outDir ?? '$root/site';  // scan target
final base = outDir ?? root;             // write target
```
Writes: in-tree at root/site/... ✓; out at outDir/blog/... ✓. Scan: in-tree at root/site ✓; out at outDir ✓.

expectedPaths in out mode: stripped 'blog/...' matching dirs 'blog/...' ✓. In-tree: full 'site/blog/...' vs dirs 'blog/...' ✗ — mismatch again for in-tree! Because _generatedPageDirs(siteDir) returns dirs relative to siteDir ('blog/x'), while in-tree expectedPaths are root-relative ('site/blog/x/index.html').

Normalize: make expectedPaths siteDir-relative in both modes:
- in-tree: rel(o) minus 'site/' prefix = 'blog/x/index.html'
- out: rel(o) already stripped.

i.e. `final prefix = 'site/'; siteRelative(o) = o.path.substring(prefix.length)` for BOTH modes (all output paths start with 'site/'). Prune compares against dirs relative to siteDir. Clean:

```dart
void emitSite({required String root, String? outDir, required List<OutputFile> outputs}) {
  final siteDir = outDir ?? '$root/site';
  if (outDir != null) _copyStaticSite(root, outDir);
  for (final o in outputs) {
    final targetPath = outDir != null ? '$outDir/${o.path}' : '$root/${o.path}';
    ...write
  }
  final expectedPaths = {for (final o in outputs) o.path.substring('site/'.length)};
  for (final dir in _generatedPageDirs(siteDir)) {
    if (!expectedPaths.any((p) => p.startsWith('$dir/'))) prune('$siteDir/$dir')
  }
```

For out mode write: '$outDir/${o.path}' would give out/site/blog/... — wrong. So write path: out mode strips 'site/': '$outDir/${o.path.substring('site/'.length)}'; in-tree: '$root/${o.path}'.

blocks.text:
One failure: styles.css missing in the out dir. Why? `_copyStaticSite` walk: `src.listSync(recursive: true)` — with recursive listing, does it include the top-level files of `site/` itself? Yes it should. Hmm — wait, `out.path` is `${root.path}-out` — the out dir is a SIBLING of the temp root, but the temp root is under /tmp... no issue there.

Ah — I see it. In the test, `out = Directory('${root.path}-out')`. `_copyStaticSite(root, outDir)` walks `$root/site`. That includes styles.css → copies to `$outDir/styles.css`... wait no: rel = 'styles.css', dest = '$outDir/styles.css'?? No — dest should be `$outDir/site/styles.css`! rel is relative to `src` = `$root/site`, so copying to `$outDir/$rel` loses the `site/` prefix!

Right: outputs are written at `$target/site/...` (paths are site-relative: 'site/blog/...'). But _copyStaticSite writes to `$outDir/$rel` where rel lacks the 'site/' prefix. Inconsistent. The out dir should contain `site/` subdir (as in FA_SITE_ROOT=$d/site). Fix: dest = `$outDir/site/$rel` and dirs `$outDir/site/$rel`.

{"newText":"      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.

blocks.text:
What happened: the auto-save committed my changes (including the trimmed blog-index template). Then — my later in-tree `dart scripts/build_site.dart` default run REGENERATED the rendered blog index in-tree (as designed, gitignored artifacts), which OVERWROTE site/blog/index.html with the rendered version! That's why the working tree shows index.html modified: the file now contains the rendered list again (unstaged modification of the committed template). Wait but the rendered index.html IS a generated artifact... should site/blog/index.html be gitignored too?? The directive said: remove "the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one)". So the template site/blog/index.html is committed with empty markers; the RENDERED version is a build product. But both live at the same path! In-tree local builds overwrite the template with the rendered version — polluting the working tree (it shows as modified, though not ignored). Options: 1. Accept: in-tree local builds dirty the template (dev must `git checkout site/blog/index.html` after). Ugly. 2. In-tree emit shouldn't write blog/index.html... but then local preview lacks the post list. 3. Make the template a separate file (e.g. site/blog/index.template.html) that the builder uses as input, and emit writes the rendered index.html. Then site/blog/index.html is fully generated (gitignore it), template committed at another path. But then a raw checkout served without building has no /blog/ index.html — acceptable? The deploy always builds. And /blog/ 404s on unbuilt local serve — but that's true for every generated page anyway. Hmm wait — but the whole site's other pages (index.html, widgets, etc.) are statics. /blog/ index being absent in a raw checkout is consistent with /blog// being absent. But careful: the builder currently reads `$root/site/blog/index.html` for markers — change to read `site/blog/index.template.html`? Hmm, that introduces a new convention. Alternatively keep markers in the committed file and DON'T write blog/index.html in-tree if it would... no, fragile. Option 3 variant with least churn: committed template stays at site/blog/index.html, and gitignore... can't ignore a tracked file. Actually — reconsider: does the in-tree default mode even need to exist? The directive's model: artifacts live at deploy/CI via --out; local dev can also use --out (e.g. `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out /tmp/site` or into site/ via --out site? hmm --out site would collide: _copyStaticSite(root, 'site') copies site/→site/ and writes blog/index.html rendered over the template — same pollution, plus skip logic prevents copying generated). The cleanest: **remove the in-tree default write of blog/index.html**? No... Alternative accepted design: keep in-tree mode (writes gitignored artifacts) but for blog/index.html specifically the file is TRACKED (template). Conflict is inherent: same path is both template (committed) and artifact (generated). The old PR had it committed as rendered artifact with markers — which the directive rejected ("rendered blog-index list" must go). So option 3 is right: introduce `site/blog/index.template.html` as the committed template; `site/blog/index.html` becomes fully generated → gitignore it; builder reads the template, writes rendered index.html. In-tree emit still writes rendered index.html (now gitignored, no pollution). Hmm wait — but then what does a plain static server of a raw checkout show at /blog/? 404 (or directory listing). Previously (before this PR) site/blog/index.html was a committed static page with the post list maintained by hand/build_blog? Let me check git history: before this PR, was site/blog/index.html committed? The PR diff added the markers... it modified site/blog/index.html (+ modifications). In the pre-PR repo, site/blog/index.html was committed (hand-maintained or build_blog-generated?). Check base version: git show HEAD~:site/blog/index.html? HEAD includes PR changes. The PR base — find merge-base. Meh. The pre-PR index.html was likely a static committed page (blog post listing) — part of the old site. If I gitignore site/blog/index.html now, the OLD committed static page gets removed from tree... The directive explicitly says: "the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one)" — i.e., remove the rendered list; keep a template. So: template at a path that doesn't clash. Decision: - New file: `site/blog/index.template.html` — committed, contains markers + empty `
`. - Builder: reads the template (buildSite), emits rendered `site/blog/index.html`. - `.gitignore`: add `site/blog/index.html`. - Remove `site/blog/index.html` from git (git rm --cached + delete? it gets regenerated at build; raw checkout lacks /blog/ page until built — consistent with all generated pages). Hmm wait — one more consideration: the crawl test "blog index lists posts without JS" serves the built tree ✓. And pages.yml --out build/pages/root: _copyStaticSite copies template (it's a static .html file at blog/index.template.html — copied ✓ harmless), generated index.html written ✓. But _copyStaticSite must NOT skip blog/index.html anymore... currently I don't skip it (only skipDirs + sitemap/llms-full) ✓ — and template gets copied too (fine, inert extra file in deploy? `index.template.html` would be deployed publicly — harmless but slightly untidy. Could skip it in copy: add skip for 'blog/index.template.html'? It'd remain accessible at /blog/index.template.html — no secret, fine. But tidier to skip. I'll skip it in _copyStaticSite. Wait, actually also: emitSite prune — `_generatedPageDirs` scans siteDir/blog for dirs with index.html — the template is a FILE, not dir ✓. In-tree emit: writes rendered site/blog/index.html (gitignored) ✓ no working-tree pollution. Also revert current polluted working tree: `git checkout -- site/blog/index.html`? The committed version (from auto-save) is my trimmed template. Then I need to MOVE it to index.template.html. Steps: 1. git show HEAD:site/blog/index.html → the trimmed template (verify). 2. Create site/blog/index.template.html from it. 3. git rm --cached site/blog/index.html (and delete file), add template. 4. Update .gitignore: add site/blog/index.html. 5. Update builder: buildSite reads `$root/site/blog/index.template.html`. 6. Update _copyStaticSite skip: 'blog/index.template.html'. 7. Update tests referencing the template path: build_site_test fixtures write 'site/blog/index.html' → change to 'site/blog/index.template.html'. 8. Check build_blog.dart or anything else referencing site/blog/index.html... grep. 9. Re-run tests + rebuild. Also check: does the auto-saved HEAD contain my older build_site.dart (pre doc-comment fix)? The unstaged build_site.dart diff (20 lines) — probably the doc-comment backtick fix + format noise. Fine. Also verify HEAD's versions of everything else are correct (ci.yml, pages.yml, .gitignore, tests). And my earlier "in-tree artifacts" are still in the working tree (gitignored): site/blog/2026.../index.html etc. — they exist locally; site/blog/index.html currently rendered. After switching to template model, rebuild in-tree to verify. Wait — one more thing about _generatedPageDirs and the copy: with template model, in a tree where dev built in-tree, site/blog contains: index.html (rendered), index.template.html, posts/, /. copyStaticSite copies index.html?? — it's a generated top-level-ish file not covered by skipDirs (dir-based) or my file skips (sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt).       # uncommittable by construction.
      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)
        run: |
          d=$(mktemp -d)

messages.preview: The auto-save committed my work, but my later in-tree build revealed a real design flaw: the committed template at `site/blog/index.html` gets overwritten by in-tree builds. The clean fix (per the dir…

blocks.text:
What happened: the auto-save committed my changes (including the trimmed blog-index template). Then — my later in-tree `dart scripts/build_site.dart` default run REGENERATED the rendered blog index in-tree (as designed, gitignored artifacts), which OVERWROTE site/blog/index.html with the rendered version! That's why the working tree shows index.html modified: the file now contains the rendered list again (unstaged modification of the committed template). Wait but the rendered index.html IS a generated artifact... should site/blog/index.html be gitignored too?? The directive said: remove "the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one)". So the template site/blog/index.html is committed with empty markers; the RENDERED version is a build product. But both live at the same path! In-tree local builds overwrite the template with the rendered version — polluting the working tree (it shows as modified, though not ignored). Options: 1. Accept: in-tree local builds dirty the template (dev must `git checkout site/blog/index.html` after). Ugly. 2. In-tree emit shouldn't write blog/index.html... but then local preview lacks the post list. 3. Make the template a separate file (e.g. site/blog/index.template.html) that the builder uses as input, and emit writes the rendered index.html. Then site/blog/index.html is fully generated (gitignore it), template committed at another path. But then a raw checkout served without building has no /blog/ index.html — acceptable? The deploy always builds. And /blog/ 404s on unbuilt local serve — but that's true for every generated page anyway. Hmm wait — but the whole site's other pages (index.html, widgets, etc.) are statics. /blog/ index being absent in a raw checkout is consistent with /blog// being absent. But careful: the builder currently reads `$root/site/blog/index.html` for markers — change to read `site/blog/index.template.html`? Hmm, that introduces a new convention. Alternatively keep markers in the committed file and DON'T write blog/index.html in-tree if it would... no, fragile. blocks.text:
What happened: the auto-save committed my changes (including the trimmed blog-index template). Then — my later in-tree `dart scripts/build_site.dart` default run REGENERATED the rendered blog index in-tree (as designed, gitignored artifacts), which OVERWROTE site/blog/index.html with the rendered version! That's why the working tree shows index.html modified: the file now contains the rendered list again (unstaged modification of the committed template). Wait but the rendered index.html IS a generated artifact... should site/blog/index.html be gitignored too?? The directive said: remove "the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one)". So the template site/blog/index.html is committed with empty markers; the RENDERED version is a build product. But both live at the same path! In-tree local builds overwrite the template with the rendered version — polluting the working tree (it shows as modified, though not ignored). Options: 1. Accept: in-tree local builds dirty the template (dev must `git checkout site/blog/index.html` after). Ugly. 2. In-tree emit shouldn't write blog/index.html... but then local preview lacks the post list. 3. Make the template a separate file (e.g. site/blog/index.template.html) that the builder uses as input, and emit writes the rendered index.html. Then site/blog/index.html is fully generated (gitignore it), template committed at another path. But then a raw checkout served without building has no /blog/ index.html — acceptable? The deploy always builds. And /blog/ 404s on unbuilt local serve — but that's true for every generated page anyway. Hmm wait — but the whole site's other pages (index.html, widgets, etc.) are statics. /blog/ index being absent in a raw checkout is consistent with /blog// being absent. But careful: the builder currently reads `$root/site/blog/index.html` for markers — change to read `site/blog/index.template.html`? Hmm, that introduces a new convention. Alternatively keep markers in the committed file and DON'T write blog/index.html in-tree if it would... no, fragile. Option 3 variant with least churn: committed template stays at site/blog/index.html, and gitignore... can't ignore a tracked file. Actually — reconsider: does the in-tree default mode even need to exist? The directive's model: artifacts live at deploy/CI via --out; local dev can also use --out (e.g. `dart scripts/build_site.dart --out /tmp/site` or into site/ via --out site? hmm --out site would collide: _copyStaticSite(root, 'site') copies site/→site/ and writes blog/index.html rendered over the template — same pollution, plus skip logic prevents copying generated). The cleanest: **remove the in-tree default write of blog/index.html**? No... Alternative accepted design: keep in-tree mode (writes gitignored artifacts) but for blog/index.html specifically the file is TRACKED (template). Conflict is inherent: same path is both template (committed) and artifact (generated). The old PR had it committed as rendered artifact with markers — which the directive rejected ("rendered blog-index list" must go). So option 3 is right: introduce `site/blog/index.template.html` as the committed template; `site/blog/index.html` becomes fully generated → gitignore it; builder reads the template, writes rendered index.html. In-tree emit still writes rendered index.html (now gitignored, no pollution). Hmm wait — but then what does a plain static server of a raw checkout show at /blog/? 404 (or directory listing). Previously (before this PR) site/blog/index.html was a committed static page with the post list maintained by hand/build_blog? Let me check git history: before this PR, was site/blog/index.html committed? The PR diff added the markers... it modified site/blog/index.html (+ modifications). In the pre-PR repo, site/blog/index.html was committed (hand-maintained or build_blog-generated?). Check base version: git show HEAD~:site/blog/index.html? HEAD includes PR changes. The PR base — find merge-base. Meh. The pre-PR index.html was likely a static committed page (blog post listing) — part of the old site. If I gitignore site/blog/index.html now, the OLD committed static page gets removed from tree... The directive explicitly says: "the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one)" — i.e., remove the rendered list; keep a template. So: template at a path that doesn't clash. Decision: - New file: `site/blog/index.template.html` — committed, contains markers + empty `
`. - Builder: reads the template (buildSite), emits rendered `site/blog/index.html`. - `.gitignore`: add `site/blog/index.html`. - Remove `site/blog/index.html` from git (git rm --cached + delete? it gets regenerated at build; raw checkout lacks /blog/ page until built — consistent with all generated pages). Hmm wait — one more consideration: the crawl test "blog index lists posts without JS" serves the built tree ✓. And pages.yml --out build/pages/root: _copyStaticSite copies template (it's a static .html file at blog/index.template.html — copied ✓ harmless), generated index.html written ✓. But _copyStaticSite must NOT skip blog/index.html anymore... currently I don't skip it (only skipDirs + sitemap/llms-full) ✓ — and template gets copied too (fine, inert extra file in deploy? `index.template.html` would be deployed publicly — harmless but slightly untidy. Could skip it in copy: add skip for 'blog/index.template.html'? It'd remain accessible at /blog/index.template.html — no secret, fine. But tidier to skip. I'll skip it in _copyStaticSite. Wait, actually also: emitSite prune — `_generatedPageDirs` scans siteDir/blog for dirs with index.html — the template is a FILE, not dir ✓. In-tree emit: writes rendered site/blog/index.html (gitignored) ✓ no working-tree pollution. Also revert current polluted working tree: `git checkout -- site/blog/index.html`? The committed version (from auto-save) is my trimmed template. Then I need to MOVE it to index.template.html. Steps: 1. git show HEAD:site/blog/index.html → the trimmed template (verify). 2. Create site/blog/index.template.html from it. 3. git rm --cached site/blog/index.html (and delete file), add template. 4. Update .gitignore: add site/blog/index.html. 5. Update builder: buildSite reads `$root/site/blog/index.template.html`. 6. Update _copyStaticSite skip: 'blog/index.template.html'. 7. Update tests referencing the template path: build_site_test fixtures write 'site/blog/index.html' → change to 'site/blog/index.template.html'. 8. Check build_blog.dart or anything else referencing site/blog/index.html... grep. 9. Re-run tests + rebuild. Also check: does the auto-saved HEAD contain my older build_site.dart (pre doc-comment fix)? The unstaged build_site.dart diff (20 lines) — probably the doc-comment backtick fix + format noise. Fine. Also verify HEAD's versions of everything else are correct (ci.yml, pages.yml, .gitignore, tests). And my earlier "in-tree artifacts" are still in the working tree (gitignored): site/blog/2026.../index.html etc. — they exist locally; site/blog/index.html currently rendered. After switching to template model, rebuild in-tree to verify. Wait — one more thing about _generatedPageDirs and the copy: with template model, in a tree where dev built in-tree, site/blog contains: index.html (rendered), index.template.html, posts/, /. copyStaticSite copies index.html?? — it's a generated top-level-ish file not covered by skipDirs (dir-based) or my file skips (sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt). It gets copied, then outputs overwrite with fresh render ✓ harmless. OK. Let me verify HEAD's template content first.

blocks.text:
What happened: the auto-save committed my changes (including the trimmed blog-index template). Then — my later in-tree `dart scripts/build_site.dart` default run REGENERATED the rendered blog index in-tree (as designed, gitignored artifacts), which OVERWROTE site/blog/index.html with the rendered version! That's why the working tree shows index.html modified: the file now contains the rendered list again (unstaged modification of the committed template). Wait but the rendered index.html IS a generated artifact... should site/blog/index.html be gitignored too?? The directive said: remove "the rendered blog-index list (keep a template/marker if the index needs one)". So the template site/blog/index.html is committed with empty markers; the RENDERED version is a build product. But both live at the same path! In-tree local builds overwrite the template with the rendered version — polluting the working tree (it shows as modified, though not ignored). Options: 1. Accept: in-tree local builds dirty the template (dev must `git checkout site/blog/index.html` after). Ugly. 2. In-tree emit shouldn't write blog/index.html... but then local preview lacks the post list. 3. Make the template a separate file (e.g. site/blog/index.template.html) that the builder uses as input, and emit writes the rendered index.html. Then site/blog/index.html is fully generated (gitignore it), template committed at another path. But then a raw checkout served without building has no /blog/ index.html — acceptable? The deploy always builds. And /blog/ 404s on unbuilt local serve — but that's true for every generated page anyway. Hmm wait — but the whole site's other pages (index.html, widgets, etc.) are statics. /blog/ index being absent in a raw checkout is consistent with /blog// being absent. But careful: the builder currently reads `$root/site/blog/index.html` for markers — change to read `site/blog/index.template.html`? Hmm, that introduces a new convention. Alternatively keep markers in the committed file and DON'T write blog/index.html in-tree if it would... no, fragile.
